messages:
anya: Hey — onboarding `open-llm/phoenix-2` failed QA, outputs are garbled even though model weights loaded. Suspect tokenizer mismatch (tokenizer.json vs tokenizer_config.json). Anyone seen fast/slow mismatch cause token id shifting?

mike: Can you paste the repo tree and the token files? Fast vs slow usually means different files present.

anya: sure, quick dump: ```ls -la repo/tokenizer/
-rw-r--r-- 1 0 0 1.2M tokenizer.json
-rw-r--r-- 1 0 0 3.2K tokenizer_config.json
-rw-r--r-- 1 0 0  123 special_tokens_map.json (missing UNK)
-rw-r--r-- 1 0 0  512 chat_templates.json
```

sasha: aha. `tokenizer.json` is the fast (tokenizers) artifact. `tokenizer_config.json` + vocab files are what slow/tokenizers from HF expect. If they disagree on special tokens or vocab_size you get id shifts and weird tokens. Common culprit: missing `unk_token` in special_tokens_map.json so fast fallback renumbers.

anya: any quick reproducer? We ran `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path)` and got a different mapping for `<|pad|>` id between fast/slow.

mike: run these locally to compare: ```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
fast = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, use_fast=True)
slow = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, use_fast=False)
print('fast', fast.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|pad|>', '<|bos|>']))
print('slow', slow.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|pad|>', '<|bos|>']))
```
If numbers differ you have mismatch. Also `tokenizer.json` can embed a different vocab (BPE merges) than files referenced in tokenizer_config.

tokenizer-bot: Scan result: tokenizer.json missing explicit `unk_token` field; tokenizer_config.json lists `unk_token: <unk>`. Potential fallback mismatch flagged.

dena: We ran into this with the `orca` bring-up. Fix was to regenerate `tokenizer.json` from the slow tokenizer to ensure identical special tokens and vocab order: ```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
slow = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, use_fast=False)
slow.save_pretrained(path)  # writes tokenizer_config.json + vocab files
# then create fast version from the same config
fast = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, use_fast=True)
fast.save_pretrained(path)
```
That caused the fast tokenizer to mirror the slow mapping.

anya: Tried that, but still saw missing `<unk>` in tokenizer.json meta. I had to ensure `special_tokens_map.json` included unk/pad/eos before saving. After adding: ```json
{"unk_token": "<unk>", "pad_token": "<|pad|>", "eos_token": "<|eos|>"}
``` and rerunning save_pretrained the ids matched.

sasha: Good. Two follow-ups: 1) add a pre-check in model-handoff that compares `vocab_size`, `all_special_tokens`, and a small token id parity test between fast/slow. 2) Add a unit in the onboarding job to synthesize fast tokenizer if missing or inconsistent. I'll open an issue.

mike: Also note: quantization evals can amplify regressions from token shifts. We saw a 3-4% perf hit in our eval metrics when a pad/unk swap happened before even running int8 quantization. So handle tokenizer parity before eval runs.

anya: Linking logs and reproducer here: https://go/phoenix-2-onboard/issue-548 (workspace).

dena: I added a tiny script to the onboarding repo that fails early if `fast.convert_tokens_to_ids(specials) != slow.convert_tokens_to_ids(specials)`. PR incoming.

tokenizer-bot: Reaction: :white_check_mark: added automated check to onboarding pipeline (staging only).

anya: Thanks — after the fix, reran full eval (n=200 prompts) and generation quality returned to baseline. Leaving a note in model-handoff checklist: always include `special_tokens_map.json` AND regenerate fast tokenizer before packaging.

mike: Great. Follow-up action items: Sasha to open infra issue for pre-check (done), Dena to submit onboarding PR (in progress), Anya to validate quantization runs post-fix and report regressions (assign to Anya).

anya: Will run int8 sweep later today and post results. TL;DR: token id parity (fast vs slow) caused garbled outputs — fix by ensuring special tokens in special_tokens_map.json and regenerating fast tokenizer from the same slow config.
